column1: # registry-limits.tsv - per-registry concurrency limits for scripts/sweep.sh
# THIS FILE IS HAND-MAINTAINED SEED DATA, NOT A GENERATED CACHE.
# bootstrap.sh must never delete or overwrite it.
#   A domain sweep is bounded by the *slowest, angriest* registry, not by your
#   CPU. Firing 32 parallel lookups at Identity Digital gets you 87 requests
#   still hanging after ten minutes; firing the same 32 at Google's pubapi RDAP
#   endpoint is completely fine. sweep.sh therefore groups work by registry
#   endpoint and gives each group its own concurrency budget, so one aggressive
#   registry throttles only its own group and can never stall the whole run.
#                 rdap:<any of above>   applies only to RDAP lookups
#                 whois:<any of above>  applies only to whois lookups
#   limit       max concurrent lookups against that registry (integer >= 1)
# PRECEDENCE (most specific wins, method-scoped breaks ties)
#   exact host  >  longest .suffix  >  *          ... and within each of those,
#   a "rdap:"/"whois:" scoped rule beats an unscoped one.
# The global -p/--parallel cap still applies on top: a group never gets more
# slots than -p, and the sum of all active groups never exceeds -p.
# Check what a host resolves to with:
# Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are ignored. If this file is missing,
# sweep.sh falls back to a small built-in table and says so loudly.
# app dev foo how day soy page new zip mov meme ing boo esq prof phd rsvp
# channel nexus. The IANA-advertised endpoint throttles hard; pubapi is
# deliberately generous and is the one lib.sh routes to.

column3: other Google Registry hosts: be conservative

column1: # No premium tier, huge infrastructure, tolerant of parallel queries.
# Moderate. Nominet has no premium tier but does rate-limit whois per source IP.
# The worst offenders by a wide margin: 87 RDAP lookups measured still hanging
# after 10 minutes. lib.sh already routes these to whois; keep them at 1 so a
# single .info-heavy list cannot consume the whole run.

column3: measured: RDAP hangs under any parallelism

column1: # Only ever queried once per TLD to discover a whois server, and serially at
# that; pinned to 1 so it can never be hammered.
# RDAP is an HTTP API built for automation; whois is a 1980s TCP service that
# most registries protect with per-IP query counters. Default accordingly.

column3: default for any RDAP endpoint not listed above
